state:
Goal `core-process-and-4-more`. `Core\Process`, `Core\Process\Handle`, `Core\Process\Result` and now `Core\Program` are green: `Core\Program` has its class card (`PROGRAM_CARD`), its three member cards are in the plain voice, and `implementing`, `implementingWith` and `id` have all their feature proofs, with perf recorded. `Core\Queue`, `Core\Queue\Id` and `Core\Queue\Stats` are untouched and still in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`.

The `implementing` attack found two leaks, both fixed and pinned. A keyless array literal, a variadic argument list and the `implementing`/`implementingWith` expansions did not free the elements already built when a later one threw (`crates/nvs-ir/src/lower/expr.rs`'s `lower_array_literal` and `lower_program_instances`, `call.rs`'s `lower_args_as_array`). They now stage each element as a transferred temporary. An object whose constructor throws was never freed (`crates/nvs-codegen/src/emit.rs`'s `emit_new`). Its error edge now releases the object before the landing block. Valgrind under WSL showed 0 bytes definitely lost for both.

A Unix-only example, or a valgrind run, is done by hand under WSL. `bun nv proofs --valgrind` needs `valgrind` on `PATH`, so it does not run on Windows. Put the commands in a script under `.agent-tmp/` and start it with `wsl.exe -- bash -lc "bash <script>"`. In the script, build with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl cargo build --bin nvs` from `/mnt/d/mwl`. Then run `/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl/debug/nvs run <file>` directly or under `valgrind --leak-check=full`. One "possibly lost" block from the TLS client cache is always there and is not a finding.
